A record field of 231 individuals and 28 teams started at Bowes Park on October 27th. We were successful in securing the "Berman" Cup, presented to the winning team in the level race, from the holders, Surrey A C.

Field, Brown and Harley, walking together, made the pace for the first two miles, when the last-named began to drop. Half-a-mile later Brown allowed the leaders to get away and so positions remained until the half-way mark.
From this point onwards Harry Churcher, who was very unlucky not to gain his Honours badge, drew away from the others, but less than 30 seconds covered Brown, Field and Harley at the finish.

Thirty teams competed and the field numbered 211. On only one occasion has this championship been won with a lower score, viz., in 1919, when the Surrey Walking Club, represented by Blackmore, Amer, Chilton and Archibald, scored 22 points only.
Ricketts Shield and Club Championship at 20 miles, which were raced for at Wimbledon on 22nd April, a small field numbering 13 only faced the starter; A.

Tommy Green led the field along at a merry pace, reaching the 5 miles mark in 40 min. 27 sec. He had opened up a gap at 10 miles (82 min. 28 sec.), increased it still further at 15 miles ( 2 hr. 3 min. 38 sec.), but between 18—19 miles was caught by A.

Latter, in particular, is deserving of our highest commendation upon finishing fifth in such a high-class field. On Whit Monday, which many will remember as a day of intense heat and tropical aridity, three of our men started in the "Guildford Cup" race over 50 kilometres (31⅛ miles) held from Croydon.

We had the certified track; the approved officials; the willing workers; a perfect day; a splendid field of first- class walkers, but—no luck!

Our twenty-milers are now training seriously and there should be a good field for the Club Championship at Wimbledon on April 21st. A prompt start will have to be made at 3 p.m. and the usual sealed handicap will be held.
The very fine field of eighteen walkers started on April 21st in the race for the "R.
Immediately following our third man, Green, were "Jock" Martin and Bert Field, giving the finest support to our scoring team that it would be possible to have.

Our usual course was used, consisting of two laps of the large field of the Common, then along Parkside to Roehampton, returning almost to the finishing point, thence a lap of the "hills" (part of our 7 miles course), and repeating these two laps to complete the 20 miles.
The "Junior" Championship for the "Savage" Shield, held on December 19th, attracted a larger field than usual; but we were sorry to miss E.

Held at Wimbledon on February 18th, and this was styled a " B " team fixture but as included in the Thames Valley team were such runners as Les Field and Alec Olney, the field was really much stronger than usual.
